newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News- Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News- Feb 26.

text.p: Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to figures released yesterday from the Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Resource Economics, Australia is on track to follow its record winter grain harvest with unprecedented summer crop production. The forecast is underpinned by expected reord cotton and rice crops and a doubling of the area sown to sunflowers. Page 2.

In a decision which signals the end of a decade-long stand-off between publishers and journalists over the ownership of reproduced articles, the Federal Court has ordered that publishers have the right to electronically reproduce articles, a move which will mean media companies will be able to better exploit the Internet. Page 2.

The Howard Government is facing an uphill battle to maintain the support of the small business constituency, with the latest update of the Yellow Pages small business index, released yesterday, showing close to 80 per cent of respondents believe the Coalition has not helped the small business sector. Page 3.

Speaking at a Public Service conference in Canberra yesterday, the secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, Max Moore-Wilton, called on the Howard Government to proceed with dramatic structural reform, including the handing of most of its service delivery functions to the private sector. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite a warning from Prime Minister John Howard on Monday that the use of mercenaries on Bougainville would be "absolutely and completely unacceptable", Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said last night a unit of 40 foreign mercenaries wold be sent into the conflict on Bougainville to advise PNG soldiers. Page 1.

Under Department of Health proposals set out in a submission this week with the Productivity Commission, which is carrying out an inquiry into the health insurance industry, older people taking out health insurance would face significantly higher premiums and longer waiting periods before claiming benefits. The Department has also backed plans to make it harder for pregnant women to claim benefits. Page 1.

Under a Federal Government plan, which has been welcomed by Australian Medical Association president Keith Woollard, parents who fail to immunise their children will lose up to A$96-a-week in benefits as well as A$200 of maternity allowance. The plan is aimed to stop children dying of preventable disease and Woollard says it will save lives. Page 1.

Under a proposed code of conduct for Australian officials serving overseas, drawn up by a Federal inquiry into allegations of paedophilia in the diplomatic service, diplomats who broke local sexual customs or became known for visiting prostitutes - even in countries where prostitution is legal - could be sent back to Australia. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under the "radical and tough" Immunise Australia program, which has been proposed by the Howard Government in an effort to boost the national level of immunisation of the young, parents will be financially penalised for failing to have their children immuised. Under the A$35 million plan, key allowances will be tied to child immunisation records. Page 1.

In a bid to avoid a potential shortfall of more than A$200 million after only selling about a third of the 35,000 stadium gold memberships, the backers of Sydney's giant Olympic stadium have resorted to selling reserved stadium seats for the Games to peope living overseas at prices well below the A$10,000 cost Australians need to pay to guarantee a stadium seat. Page 1.

Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has told A Current Affair his Government has been trying to recruit an elite armed squad for the past 18 months, but he denied Sandline International, a British-registered company, would be used as a mercenary force to launch an assault on Bougainville. Page 1.

Andrew Grech, a partner in Melbourne law firm Slater and Gordon, which was responsible for a class action on behalf of 800 consumers affected by last year's salmonella outbreak, confirmed last night his firm has been briefed to conduct a similar action aginst those responsible for the Wallis Lake hepatitis A outbreak. Page 2.
THE AGE

A scheme unveiled yesterday by Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge, would reward parents who immunised their children and penalise those who did not. Parents who fail to immunise their children will lose their child-care assistance and will suffer a cut in maternity allowance. Page 1.

Dismissing demands by Australian leaders that Papua New Guinea abandon its plans to send mercenaries to Bougainville Island, Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan last night confirmed his plans, saying the group of about 40 highly trained combat fighters would advise PNG forces on the island, but would not really be on the front line. Page 1.

Speaking at a Victorian Employers Chamber of Commerce and Industry summit on the State's future yesterday, Victorian Industry, Science and Technology Minister Mark Birrell hit out at the Commonwealth over cuts to research and development subsidies and higer education charges, branding the R&D changes "plain destructive". Page 1.

Responding to a series of highly damaging child-sex allegations against Australian diplomats, a Federal inquiry into paedophilia has proposed a code of conduct which would see Australian diplomats on overseas postings able to have sex with a prostitute aslong as they could not be identified or recognised as a representative of the country, but would be banned from any public display of affection that might offend the local community. Page 1.
